Should You Invest in Alphabet?. Alphabet sits at the intersection of global digital transformation and artificial intelligence disruption. This makes it one of the most closely watched companies right now. With Google Search, YouTube, and Google Cloud as its main engines, Alphabet continues to shape how billions of users access information, connect, and work. The company’s relentless push into generative AI and cloud-based productivity fuels its own growth and sets the pace for the entire technology sector. As a technology conglomerate, Alphabet’s core business spans digital advertising, cloud computing, and an expanding suite of hardware products and “Other Bets.” Google Services, including search, YouTube, and Android, remain the backbone. Google Cloud has cemented Alphabet’s position as a leader in enterprise AI and infrastructure. It directly competes with Amazon and Microsoft as businesses race to modernize IT operations. The company’s global scale and deep research and development pipeline keep it well ahead of smaller competitors. Its brand power continues to attract both users and developers. Financially, Alphabet sets a high bar for large-cap tech. The company delivered $96.4 billion in revenue and $28.2 billion in net income in the June 2025 quarter, up 13.8% and 22.3% year over year, respectively. Operating and profit margins reached 32% and 29.2% respectively in the June 2025 quarter, which shows a business model with enviable efficiency and pricing power. Alphabet’s balance sheet remains strong, with over $21 billion in cash and $362.9 billion in shareholder equity as of June 2025. Alphabet accelerated investments in cloud and AI. The company also increased capital expenditures. However, management continues to generate strong free cash flow and began paying a dividend in 2024 for added shareholder return. What truly sets Alphabet apart is its ability to consistently innovate at scale. Alphabet deploys AI capabilities across Search, drives monetization on YouTube, and leverages its cloud platform for the next wave of business transformation. The company’s ecosystem gives it a long runway for growth. Alphabet’s scale, brand, and cash generation support aggressive investment in new opportunities. It also returns capital to shareholders. For investors seeking enduring growth potential in a dynamic technology landscape, we believe Alphabet offers a compelling mix of stability, upside, and optionality. The challenge, as always, lies in finding companies with similar long-term prospects in a dynamic market.

Title: French Data Watchdog Fines Google, Shein Record $553
Full_Text: French Data Watchdog Fines Google, Shein Record $553.9 Million Over Cookies Published: Sept. 4, 2025 at 4:33 a.m. ET Share Resize By Edith Hancock France's data protection authority fined Alphabet's Google and Shein a total 475 million euros ($553.9 million) over concerns the companies are flouting French regulations around cookies. The CNIL said late Wednesday that it fined Google 325 million euros and Shein 150 million euros respectively, as part of the regulator's broader attempt to regulate how large technology companies use cookies to track users online. It said that Google should have asked for users' consent to display adverts in emails through Gmail's "Promotions" and "Social" tabs, saying that it believes 53 million individuals had illegally been served adverts in those tabs. The CNIL also said that advertising cookies were placed on the devices of users visiting Shein's website when they landed on the page and before they were able to choose a preference for tracking. It added that both companies didn't adequately inform users they were being tracked for advertising. A Google spokesperson said the company is reviewing the decision. Shein said it contests the verdict and will appeal it.
